text: When does The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth come out?. The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth opens in IMAX theaters on Nov. 25, 2026, for an exclusive two-week run, then streams on Netflix starting Dec. 23, 2026. David Fincher directed the film from a script by Quentin Tarantino, with Brad Pitt returning as Cliff Booth from Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.. Searches for the Brad Pitt sequel are climbing ahead of its Nov. 25, 2026, IMAX debut.. Netflix confirmed the dates on its Tudum site: an exclusive two-week global IMAX engagement starting Nov. 25, 2026, followed by the Netflix release on Dec. 23. The film was long known as The Adventures of Cliff Booth before it was retitled The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth in August 2026. Many people search for it as "The Misadventures of Cliff Booth." The story is set in 1977, eight years after Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. Cliff now works as a fixer for Hollywood's elite. A talent agent, Karen Crosby (Elizabeth Debicki), hires him on behalf of Charlie Peters (Scott Caan), a TV star known for doing his own stunts. As Cliff is drawn into Charlie's circle, the story shifts into a crime thriller, according to Netflix. The cast also includes Carla Gugino as Toni, Charlie's wife; Yahya Abdul-Mateen II as Roderick "Hot Rod" Harrison, a former pro football champion turned actor; Matt Groove and JB Tadena as the Verdusco brothers; and Peter Weller, Corey Fogelmanis and Karren Karagulian.

Does MLB have a salary cap? No, but owners want one by 2028. No. Major League Baseball has no salary cap, unlike the NFL, NBA and NHL. Teams can spend as much as they want on players. In November 2026, owners proposed a cap of $258.2 million and a floor of $180.2 million starting in 2028, and the players union calls a cap a non-starter.. MLB owners have put a salary cap on the table in talks with the players union before the labor deal expires on Dec. 1, 2026.. MLB said on Nov. 3, 2026, that it was proposing to phase in a salary cap and a payroll floor in 2028, Field Level Media reported. MLB said 12 clubs would have to add a combined $636 million in payroll to reach the floor, and eight clubs would have to cut a combined $528 million to get under the cap. Owners have also proposed limiting any one player to 15% of a team's payroll, the. The union opposes the idea. Interim executive director Bruce Meyer said caps "suffocate competition by offering owners an all-purpose excuse for inaction and mediocrity." The last time owners pushed for a cap, in 1994, it led to a 7 1/2-month strike and the first canceled World Series in 90 years. The current labor deal was reached on day 99 of a lockout in 2022. The five-year collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, 2026, at 10:59 p.m. CT, and a lockout is expected if there is no deal. Players instead want expanded free agency and arbitration, a nearly doubled minimum salary, more revenue sharing and a tax on teams with payrolls below a set level.

Is Guarding Stars based on a book? Yes, Katherine Center's The Bodyguard. Yes. Netflix's Guarding Stars, starring Leighton Meester and Jared Padalecki, is based on Katherine Center's 2022 novel The Bodyguard. It keeps the book's leads, bodyguard Hannah Brooks and movie star Jack Stapleton, but moves the story from Texas to Montana. It premieres on Netflix on Nov. 18, 2026.. Guarding Stars, Netflix's adaptation of Katherine Center's The Bodyguard, premieres Nov. 18, 2026.. In the film, Hannah Brooks is a no-nonsense security agent assigned to protect Jack Stapleton, a movie star who is being stalked. The two pose as a couple while he spends the holidays at his family's ranch, and the act turns into a real romance, according to Netflix. The book's leads have the same names. Meester plays Hannah and Padalecki plays Jack. The film was called The Bodyguard during production. The biggest change reported so far is the setting: the novel is set in Texas, while the film is set in Montana, according to What's on Netflix. Elizabeth Allen Rosenbaum directed, from a script by Erin Cardillo, Richard Keith, Gina Matthews and Grant Scharbo. Filming took place in Calgary, Alberta, from Dec. 4, 2025, to February 2026, with additional shooting in Vancouver. The cast also includes Andie MacDowell, country singer Walker Hayes in his acting debut, Noah LaLonde, Toby Sandeman, Rachael Ancheril, wrestler Phil Brooks (CM Punk), singer Ava Max and Shaun Johnston.

Is How to Rob a Bank a true story? The 2026 Nicholas Hoult movie. The 2026 movie How to Rob a Bank, starring Nicholas Hoult, is a heist action comedy written by Mark Bianculli, and its studio descriptions and director interviews don't credit any real case. The true story with the same title is a different film: Netflix's 2024 documentary about 1990s Seattle-area bank robber Scott Scurlock.. David Leitch's heist comedy How to Rob a Bank, with Nicholas Hoult and Zoë Kravitz, opens in U.S. Theaters on Nov. 13, 2026.. How to Rob a Bank, directed by David Leitch (Bullet Train, The Fall Guy), opens in U.S. Theaters on Nov. 13, 2026, from Amazon MGM Studios. It was first set for Sept. 4, 2026. Its premise, as Complex described it in a Nov. 2 interview with Leitch, follows "a viral group of bank robbers that share their exploits on YouTube for the world to see." Leitch said he had "always wanted to do a heist movie." The cast includes Nicholas Hoult as Ryan, Zoë Kravitz as Reagan Gardner, Pete Davidson as Vince, John C. Reilly as Agent West, Christian Slater as Walton and Tati Gabrielle as Skyler, with Anna Sawai and Rhenzy Feliz. Filming began in Pittsburgh in June 2025, and the movie runs 122 minutes. The name causes confusion because Netflix released a documentary called How to Rob a Bank in 2024. That film tells the real story of Scott Scurlock, who carried out a string of bank robberies in the Seattle area in the 1990s. The two films are unrelated.

What does maxxing mean? Dictionary.com's 2026 Word of the Year. Maxxing means pursuing an activity to the fullest or optimizing some part of your life. It works on its own ("I'm maxxing everything") or as a suffix, as in looksmaxxing or sleepmaxxing. Dictionary.com named maxxing its 2026 Word of the Year.. Dictionary.com named maxxing its 2026 Word of the Year on Oct. 25, 2026.. Dictionary.com traces maxxing to maximum, maximize and max, and to the gaming term min-maxing, which means building a character's strengths so its weaknesses don't matter. The word picked up an extra "x" and first spread on Reddit and other forums. People also type it as "maxing," but the double-x spelling is the one Dictionary.com chose. The most familiar form is looksmaxxing, trying to improve your physical appearance. Dictionary.com said searches for looksmaxxing "skyrocketed in early 2026" and searches for maxxing on its own "have risen exponentially over the past year." Other examples it lists include tokenmaxxing (using as much AI at work as possible), nonnamaxxing (adopting an Italian grandmother's habits) and cozymaxxing. The other words on Dictionary.com's 2026 shortlist were affordability, data center, odyssey and unc.

What does unc mean? The slang term Gen Z uses for "uncool". In current slang, "unc" means someone who is out of touch or uncool, often an older person who "just doesn't get it." It is a clipping of "uncle." Dictionary.com put unc on its 2026 Word of the Year shortlist and compared it to "OK Boomer.". Dictionary.com named unc to its 2026 Word of the Year shortlist, announced Oct. 25, 2026.. Unc comes from African American Vernacular English, where it was used affectionately or respectfully for an older man in the family or a mentor, according to Dictionary.com. In 2026, Gen Z and Gen Alpha began using it as a jab at anyone who seems corny or behind the times. Dictionary.com put it this way: "Think of it like the new 'OK Boomer,' signifying that Gen Z is now the driving force of culture." The tone depends on who is talking. Among friends or family it can still be warm, a nickname for an uncle or an older friend. Aimed at a stranger, it usually means "you're old and out of touch." It is also written in all capitals, "UNC," which is not the same as the abbreviation for the University of North Carolina. Unc made Dictionary.com's 2026 shortlist alongside affordability, data center and odyssey. The winner was maxxing.

What is a motion to table? How the House kills a measure fast. A motion to table is a quick, no-debate vote that kills a measure in the House. If a majority votes to table, the proposal is effectively dead, the same as if it had been voted down. Republican leaders could use one against Rep. Thomas Massie's resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.. House Republican leaders could move to table Rep. Thomas Massie's resolution to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth when it reaches the floor in November 2026.. House Practice, the official guide to House procedure, says tabling is "equivalent to a final adverse disposition" of a measure, not a temporary pause as "tabling" can mean in everyday speech or in some other bodies. The motion "is not debatable," so members vote on it right away. It can be made after a proposition is called up but before debate begins, and it is no longer in order once the previous question or the yeas and nays have been ordered. A tabled matter generally returns only by unanimous consent or a suspension of the rules. Because any member can force a privileged resolution, such as articles of impeachment, to the floor, the motion to table gives the House a way to dispose of one without voting on its substance. Motions to table or refer a privileged resolution are in order, according to the Congressional Research Service. On Nov. 9, 2026, that GOP leaders could move to table Massie's impeachment resolution against Hegseth instead of voting on the eight articles. Tabling needs a simple majority, the same as passage, so the outcome turns on how many Republicans join Democrats.

What is a privileged resolution? How Massie can force a Hegseth vote. A privileged resolution is a measure the House must deal with quickly, without waiting for committee action or leadership approval. When a rank-and-file member offers one, the House has to take it up within two legislative days. Rep. Thomas Massie is using this route to force a vote on impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.. Rep. Thomas Massie says he will refile his privileged impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth after the House returned on Nov. 9, 2026, forcing a floor vote within two legislative days.. Under House Rule IX, a member can rise "to a question of the privileges of the House" and send a resolution to the clerk's desk, where it is read aloud. If the majority or minority leader offers it, the speaker rules on it right away. If any other member offers it, the speaker can put it off, but only to a time "within the next two legislative days," according to the Congressional Research Service. Impeachment resolutions are also privileged, and Bloomberg Government and ABC News report that the same two-legislative-day clock applies to Massie's. Once a privileged resolution comes up, the House can debate it for an hour, vote on it directly, or vote on a motion to table or refer it, which can end it without a vote on the merits. Massie, a Kentucky Republican, first offered eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth as a privileged resolution on Sept. 15, 2026, Bloomberg Government reported. The articles accuse Hegseth of exceeding his constitutional authority and violating congressional war powers. No vote happened: Speaker Mike Johnson canceled the last scheduled legislative day before the midterms, and Massie told ABC News on Sept. 16 that he would have to refile when Congress returned. On Nov. 9 that Massie could reintroduce the resolution "as soon as Monday," which would start the two-day clock again. Massie lost his Republican primary and leaves Congress in January. Even if the House impeached Hegseth, removal would take a two-thirds vote in the Senate, which ABC called unlikely.

What is Dandori Academy? Pikmin 4's new Switch 2 mode. Dandori Academy is a new challenge mode in Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy, out Nov. 12, 2026. It adds 72 "Dandori exam" stages that test how efficiently you command your Pikmin, with three difficulty levels, medals and online leaderboards.. Pikmin 4 – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy launches Nov. 12, 2026.. "Dandori" is the Pikmin series' word for planning and multitasking, which Nintendo describes as "the art of commanding your Pikmin effectively." Dandori Academy turns that into a series of exams. Gematsu reported that the 72 stages vary in difficulty, earn players in-game medals, and "will be released over time." Nintendo Wire reported that new exams arrive every Friday, Saturday and Sunday, and that online leaderboards let players compare scores with friends and strangers. The Switch 2 Edition also lets players challenge friends in Dandori Battles on the same system, or through GameShare locally or online via GameChat, even if the friend doesn't own the game. Players can give voice commands to Oatchi, the player's dog companion, through the Switch 2 microphone, and the game runs with sharper, higher-resolution visuals in TV and handheld modes. Yoshiaki Koizumi announced the edition in a Nintendo Direct on Sept. 9, 2026. Owners of the original Switch version can buy a digital upgrade, as with earlier Switch 2 Editions, and a new cartridge contains everything.

What is the Bearista cup? Starbucks' mystery bear cups, explained. The Bearista is Starbucks' bear-shaped glass cold cup: a bear in a winter cap, in Starbucks green, with the cap as the lid. It sold out within hours in November 2025. For 2026, Starbucks is selling mystery "Surprise Box" Bearistas starting Nov. 10, and the original Bearista returns to select U.S. Stores on Dec. 1, while supplies last.. Starbucks' mystery Bearista Surprise Boxes go on sale Nov. 10, 2026, a year after the original cup sold out in hours.. The first Bearista Glass Cold Cup, a 20-ounce glass cup shaped like a bear in a winter cap, in Starbucks' signature green, went on sale on Nov. 6, 2025, for $29.95, Quartz reported. It sold out within hours, some stores got only one or two, and resale listings on eBay and Mercari ranged from $150 to more than $1,000. Starbucks apologized, saying "excitement for our merchandise exceeded even our biggest expectations." On Oct. 26, 2026, Starbucks said the Bearista was coming back with a twist. The Surprise Box Edition goes on sale Nov. 10 in limited quantities: each box holds a mystery glass Bearista, and buyers find out which design they got only when they open it. The original Bearista returns to select U.S. Coffeehouses on Dec. 1. Reports did not list 2026 prices or purchase limits. The cups are part of Starbucks' holiday season lineup. Red Cup Day, when customers get a free reusable cup with an eligible handcrafted holiday drink, is Nov. 17, 2026, the same day a Winter Wonderland drinkware collection launches.
